Short answer: No, meals are generally not deductible unless specific conditions are met [26 U.S.C. § 274(k)-(l)], [26 U.S.C. § 274(n)(1)], [26 CFR 1.274-12(c)(1)].

No deduction shall be allowed under this chapter for the expense of any food or beverages unless the expense is not lavish or extravagant under the circumstances, and the taxpayer (or an employee of the taxpayer) is present at the furnishing of such food or beverages [26 U.S.C. § 274(k)-(l)]. Only 50 percent of meal expenses is allowed as a deduction [26 U.S.C. § 274(n)(1)]. Food or beverage expenses are subject to limitations unless they fall under specific exceptions provided in regulations [26 CFR 1.274-12(c)(1)]. Food or beverages means all food and beverage items, regardless of whether characterized as meals, snacks, or other types of food and beverages [26 CFR 1.274-12(b)(1)].

Short answer: It depends: meals may be deductible if they meet specific criteria [26 U.S.C. § 274(k)-(l)], [26 U.S.C. § 274(n)(1)], [26 CFR 1.274-12(a)(4)].

No deduction shall be allowed for the expense of any food or beverages unless the expense is not lavish or extravagant under the circumstances and the taxpayer (or an employee of the taxpayer) is present at the furnishing of such food or beverages [26 U.S.C. § 274(k)-(l)]. Only 50 percent of meal expenses is allowed as a deduction [26 U.S.C. § 274(n)(1)]. Food or beverage expenses paid or incurred while traveling away from home in pursuit of a trade or business are subject to deduction limitations and substantiation requirements [26 CFR 1.274-12(a)(4)].
